title: Amit Goffer, paralyzed in all four limbs, invented ReWalk: a robotic skeleton that brings disabled people back to walking

trailer.text: Dr. Amit Goffer, an Israeli entrepreneur and Technion graduate, founded Odin after retiring from Elbit, a medical company that specialized in building MRI machines.
Amit Goffer is an Israeli entrepreneur who became paralyzed in all four limbs after a serious all-terrain vehicle accident.
After rehabilitation he saw on the internet that there was no alternative to the wheelchair, and then he came up with the idea of ReWalk.
He founded the Argo company to create a product that would enable people with spinal cord injuries to walk again.
ReWalk was the first motorized exoskeleton to receive FDA approval.
According to Calcalist, Goffer himself will not be among those helped by his invention.

glance.label: Offices
glance.value: Marlborough, Massachusetts; Berlin; and Yokneam Illit.

glance.label: Users
glance.value: About 400 worldwide, according to an undated JNS article.

paragraphs.text: Goffer said that in the accident something went wrong with the brakes of the all-terrain vehicle.
He veered off the track, hit a tree and broke his neck.
According to what he told Globes, his daughter was with him and was thrown to one side, and he himself flew into the tree.
Already at the moment of the accident, still at the scene, Goffer understood that he was paralyzed.
He was left paralyzed in all four limbs.
Nine months after the accident he returned to his home in Tivon from the long rehabilitation at Tel HaShomer.
Goffer said that he decided to stop taking the painkillers, and suddenly everything became clear.
He did not understand why a wheelchair is the only solution and why there is no device that leads people.
He saw on the internet that there was no alternative to the wheelchair, and then he came up with the idea of ReWalk.
According to Calcalist, hundreds of failed attempts to stand paralyzed people up and make them walk are documented in medical history.
Goffer said that no one believed him and that he was treated like a madman.
Before that he founded Odin, a medical company that specialized in building MRI machines, after retiring from Elbit.
According to Calcalist, Goffer began working on ReWalk in 1998.
The device can help only those whose hands are not paralyzed and who can use crutches, and not quadriplegics like him.

stations.title: From an idea to a company

paragraphs.text: Goffer founded Argo Medical Technologies in 2001.
Venture capital firms refused to invest in him.
The Chief Scientist trusted him, and in 2003 agreed to add one shekel from state funds for every shekel Goffer would bring.
About two years later Argo entered the Technion incubator.
There it turned the first model into a working prototype.
In an interview with Calcalist, conducted before FDA approval in the United States, Goffer said the company had raised about $5 million up to that point.
According to the IVC database, the Vitalife fund invested about one and a half million dollars in it.
A report on CNN brought Goffer international publicity.
Following it came foreign newspapers and television networks.
A slight tilt of the upper body activates the metal legs.
Walking is done with the help of ordinary crutches.
Goffer said that the person directs the system using a device with buttons on the wrist, and the device does not lead him.
According to the company's website, the device requires the ability to use the upper limbs, and normal heart-lung function and bone density.
According to JNS, people with paralysis have very weak bones, so ReWalk recommends avoiding slippery, sloped or uneven surfaces.
According to Goffer, the walking is close to normal walking.
According to the company, the ReWalk Personal exoskeleton is the only personal exoskeleton FDA-cleared for use on stairs and curbs.
Radi Kaiuf, the device's test pilot, was hit by two bullets in his back during his military service in Lebanon.
According to Globes, he was wounded on May 3, 1988, when Paratrooper Battalion 202 raided the town of Maidun.
He was left paralyzed from the waist down and was bound to a wheelchair for 20 years.
According to Goffer, Kaiuf walked 10 kilometers in the Tel Aviv Marathon with the device with no problem.
Kaiuf said that when you stand you see the world at your normal height, and that this restores self-respect.
According to Goffer, test user Radi Kaiof told him that his daughter had told him that at last she sees him at eye level, like a real father.
Captain Derek Herrera of the U.S. Marine Corps, who was paralyzed in Afghanistan, trained with the ReWalk device.
He wrote that the technology changed his life for the better, physically, emotionally and psychologically.
According to JNS, there are about 400 users around the world, including American veterans and law-enforcement officials.
The product received the European CE approval, and according to Goffer its marketing in Italy by a rehabilitation center began in 2010.
The ReWalk Personal was launched in 2012 and is available throughout Europe.
On June 26, 2014, Argo announced the FDA approval, which allows the device to be purchased for private use.
According to Scientific American, it is the first wearable exoskeleton approved for home use.
The company's CEO, Larry Jasinski, said that the product would have an immediate, life-changing impact on people with spinal cord injuries.
According to the Jerusalem Post, studies have shown that users improve their cardiovascular health and their muscle and digestive system performance.
In December 2015 the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs agreed to pay for exoskeletons for eligible veterans with spinal-cord injuries.
According to Globes, the department will establish 24 centers to evaluate the ability of the injured to use the system.
On April 11, 2024, Medicare finalized the reimbursement for personal exoskeletons.
President Barack Obama viewed the device during his visit to Israel.
According to MedicalXpress, ReWalk won best invention awards from Popular Science and Time.
Argo grew from a small start-up in Israel into an international company with headquarters in the United States, Germany and Israel.

According to Globes (January 2016), after declining gradually for about 15 months since the IPO, the share price jumped 90% in a single day about two weeks before the article was published, following the announcement by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, and at the time of publication it stood at almost $14.50.

stations.title: The next step: standing on wheels

paragraphs.text: Goffer was the company's CEO from 2001 to 2012, and from 2012 to 2015 he was its president and CTO.
According to a 2014 article by the American Technion Society, Goffer was at that time working on UPnRIDE.
It is an upright device on wheels that will allow wheelchair users to move while standing.

stations.title: Price, insurance and IDF disabled veterans

paragraphs.text: According to JNS, most insurance companies in the United States refused to cover the device.
In 2017 the State of Florida Division of Administrative Hearings ruled that Blue Cross Blue Shield of Florida must cover a ReWalk system for a plan member with a spinal cord injury.
According to JNS, Goffer and other experts believe that insurance companies could have saved about $30,000 per patient per year.

Even in Israel, where it was invented, the device had not reached IDF disabled veterans as of 2016; in April 2025 the company reported a paralyzed soldier, the first injured in the war to walk again with it, and said the Rehabilitation Department is evaluating it for other veterans.
The parties involved described this in several different ways.

Scientific American: an ATV accident in 1997

Globes: yes, using a unique algorithm for lifting the legs
Jerusalem Post: reportedly, the device is not suitable for going up stairs

disagreements.question: How many training sessions are needed?

Ministry of Defense: the matter did not work out for various reasons

claims.text: ב-2014 משרד ענייני החיילים המשוחררים האמריקאי הסכים לשלם עבור שלדים חיצוניים לחיילים משוחררים זכאים עם פגיעות חוט שדרה.
claims.quote: In 2014, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs agreed to pay the cost of exoskeletons for eligible veterans with spinal-cord injuries.

claims.text: לפי גלובס, משרד ענייני החיילים המשוחררים האמריקאי יקים 24 מרכזים בארצות הברית שיבדקו את יכולת פצועי חוט שדרה להשתמש במערכת.
claims.quote: will establish 24 centers all over the US to evaluate the ability of people with spinal cord injuries to use the system

claims.text: ב-11 באפריל 2024 מדיקר סיים את קביעת ההחזר עבור שלדים חיצוניים אישיים.
claims.quote: On April 11, 2024, Medicare finalized its reimbursement for personal exoskeletons.

claims.text: נשיא ארצות הברית ברק אובמה צפה במכשיר בביקורו בישראל בשנה הקודמת.

claims.text: לפי מדיקל אקספרס, ReWalk זכה בפרסי ההמצאה הטובה ביותר מהמגזינים Popular Science ו-Time.
claims.quote: which has won "best invention" awards from Popular Science and Time magazines

claims.text: במהלך העשור שחלף ארגו גדלה מסטארט-אפ קטן שבסיסו בישראל לחברה בינלאומית עם מטה בארצות הברית, בגרמניה ובישראל.
claims.quote: Over the past decade, Argo has grown from a small research and development start-up based in Israel to an international company with headquarters in the US, Germany, and Israel.

claims.text: מחיר המניה זינק ב-90% ביום אחד והגיע לכמעט 14.50 דולר.

claims.text: גופר עובד כיום על UPnRIDE, מכשיר זקוף על גלגלים שיאפשר למשתמשי כיסא גלגלים להיות ניידים בעמידה.
claims.quote: Currently, Dr. Goffer is at work on UPnRIDE, a product that would improve the quality of life for all wheelchair users.

claims.text: לפי JNS, ReWalk עולה כ-70,000 דולר, ורוב חברות הביטוח בארצות הברית סירבו לכסות אותו.
claims.quote: Because ReWalk costs approximately $70,000, many who could benefit from using it cannot afford it.

claims.text: ביוני 2017 בית משפט בפלורידה קבע שחברת הביטוח Blue Cross Blue Shield of Florida חייבת לכסות מערכת ReWalk עבור מבוטח עם פגיעת חוט שדרה.

claims.text: לפי JNS, גופר ומומחים נוספים מאמינים שחברות ביטוח יכלו לחסוך כ-30,000 דולר למטופל בשנה.
claims.quote: Goffer and other experts believe insurance providers could save approximately $30,000 per patient annually

claims.text: לדברי גופר, בישראל שבה הומצא המכשיר נכי צה"ל יישארו ישובים בכיסא גלגלים בעוד שבעולם ילכו.

claims.quote: ReWalk was invented after a tractor accident in 1997 left Dr. Goffer a quadriplegic.

claims.quote: This is done through a unique algorithm for picking up the legs differently.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, על פי דיווחים המכשיר אינו מתאים לעלייה במדרגות.
claims.quote: However, it is reportedly not suitable for going up stairs.

claims.text: לפי מדיקל אקספרס, המשתמש צריך כוח בפלג הגוף העליון ולעבור כ-15 מפגשי אימון בני שעה כדי ללמוד ללכת.
claims.quote: Users must have upper body strength to manipulate crutches, (making ReWalk unsuitable for quadriplegics), and undergo some 15 one-hour training sessions to learn to walk.

claims.text: לפי JNS, לימוד השימוש בשלד החיצוני לוקח בדרך כלל בין 12 ל-15 מפגשים.
claims.quote: It generally takes somewhere between 12 and 15 sessions to learn how to use the exoskeleton.

claims.text: ג'רוזלם פוסט כתב שקפטן דרק האררה (בכתיב "Harare") ממארינס ארצות הברית, שמתאמן עם ReWalk, יהיה בין האמריקאים הראשונים שירכשו אותו.
claims.quote: Derek Harare, a paraplegic in the US Marine Corps who has been training with ReWalk, will be one of the first Americans to buy one.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, הדיווחים בתקשורת מעמידים את מחיר המכשיר על 65,000 עד 68,000 דולר.

quote_translations.c2: Amit Goffer, an Israeli entrepreneur and start-up founder who more than a decade ago became paralyzed in all four limbs following a serious all-terrain vehicle accident
quote_translations.c14: I went on the internet and saw that there was no alternative at all to the wheelchair, and then I came up with the idea of ReWalk
quote_translations.c17: his new life as a disabled person, the invention grew that may help millions of disabled people around the world. Ironically, Goffer himself will not be among them.
quote_translations.c21: Goffer began working on the development of ReWalk by himself as early as 1998, a year after the serious accident he had
quote_translations.c9: and then something went wrong with the brakes of the all-terrain vehicle I was driving, I veered off the track, hit a tree and broke my neck
quote_translations.c11: Already at the moment of the accident, still at the scene, Goffer understood that he was paralyzed.
quote_translations.c12: Nine months later Goffer returned to his home in Tivon from the long rehabilitation at Tel HaShomer
quote_translations.c13: and then I decided to stop taking all the painkillers they had given me - and suddenly everything became clear
quote_translations.c15: I didn't understand why a wheelchair is the only solution, why there is no device that simply leads people.
quote_translations.c4: hundreds of failed attempts to stand paralyzed people up and make them walk are documented in medical history
quote_translations.c18: No one believed me either, and they treated me like a madman.
quote_translations.c20: a medical start-up that he founded after retiring from Elbit and that specialized in building MRI machines
quote_translations.c16: Your device can help only those whose hands are not paralyzed and who can use crutches, not quadriplegics like you.
quote_translations.c24: Venture capital firms, which Goffer does not want to name, also refused to invest in him
quote_translations.c22: Only the Chief Scientist trusted him, and in 2003 agreed to put one shekel from state funds for every shekel Goffer would bring
quote_translations.c23: About two years later Argo was already operating in the Technion incubator, where it turned the first model into a working prototype
quote_translations.c26: According to Goffer, over the years the company raised about $5 million.
quote_translations.c27: According to IVC, the database of the Israeli high-tech industry, Vitalife invested about one and a half million dollars in Argo
quote_translations.c25: One report on CNN bought him international publicity, and following it came more foreign newspapers and television networks

quote_translations.c36: In addition to the ability to use the upper limbs, the device requires normal heart-lung function and bone density
quote_translations.c32: ReWalk enables walking that is close to normal walking, and even enables going up and down stairs and moving over rough terrain
